title: About this sample knowledge base
text: This sample is a set of short notes on technology and US stock market changes since 2020. It is built from public sources, mainly Wikipedia articles, retrieved on 2026-11-09. It is not proprietary research and not investment advice. Figures were summarised from the cited pages and have not been independently verified.

title: The 2020 stock market crash: how fast stocks fell in February 2020
text: The 2020 stock market crash began on 20 February 2020 and ended on 7 April 2020. US indices fell at least 10% over 24 to 28 February 2020, which Wikipedia calls the fastest correction from an all-time high in market history, taking six days. The Dow entered a bear market on 11 March 2020, the first in 11 years. US indices did not return to January 2020 levels until November 2020. Source: Wikipedia, 2020 stock market crash.

title: The worst days of March 2020
text: The Dow fell 7.79% on 9 March 2020, 9.99% on 12 March and 12.93% on 16 March, closing at 20,188.52. The S&P 500 closed down 9.5% on 12 March and fell 12 to 13% on 16 March. The Nasdaq closed down 9.4% on 12 March. Trading curbs, also called circuit breakers, triggered on 9, 12, 16 and 18 March 2020. Source: Wikipedia, 2020 stock market crash.

title: VIX volatility index record in March 2020
text: The VIX volatility index closed at 82.69 on 16 March 2020, the highest closing value on record. Intraday peaks in 2008 were higher. Source: Wikipedia, 2020 stock market crash.

title: Federal Reserve (Fed) emergency rate cuts in March 2020
text: The Federal Reserve cut its target range for the federal funds rate to 1% to 1.25% on 3 March 2020. After an emergency unscheduled meeting on 15 March 2020 the range was 0% to 0.25%. Source: Wikipedia, History of Federal Open Market Committee actions.

title: S&P 500 stock market annual returns and performance 2019 to 2021
text: The S&P 500 price return was 28.88% in 2019, 16.26% in 2020 and 26.89% in 2021. Including dividends, total returns were 31.49%, 18.40% and 28.71%. Source: Wikipedia, S&P 500.

title: S&P 500 stock market annual returns and performance 2022 to 2025
text: The S&P 500 price return was -19.44% in 2022, 24.23% in 2023, 23.31% in 2024 and 16.39% in 2025. Including dividends, total returns were -18.11%, 26.29%, 25.02% and 17.88%. Source: Wikipedia, S&P 500.

title: The GameStop short squeeze of January 2021
text: GameStop began January 2021 at $17.25. Its pre-market price briefly topped $500 on 28 January 2021, nearly 30 times that start, before a later split adjustment. The all-time intraday high was $483.00 as of 28 January 2021, about 190 times the $2.57 low of April 2020. Reddit users on r/wallstreetbets drove the squeeze. Source: Wikipedia, GameStop short squeeze.

title: GameStop short interest and the losers
text: About 140% of GameStop's public float had been sold short by 22 January 2021. Short interest fell to 15% by 24 March 2021. Melvin Capital lost 53% of its investments by the end of January 2021 and shut down on 18 May 2022. Short sellers reportedly lost $6 billion by 26 January 2021. Source: Wikipedia, GameStop short squeeze.

title: Why Robinhood stopped and halted GameStop trades: trading restrictions
text: On 28 January 2021 Robinhood halted new purchases of GameStop, AMC, BlackBerry, Nokia and other volatile stocks, though customers could still sell. Robinhood and others said clearing houses had raised collateral requirements, and the DTCC raised industry requirements from $26 billion to $33.5 billion. Robinhood faced 34 class-action lawsuits as of 2 February 2021. A House Financial Services hearing on 18 February 2021 questioned Robinhood's and Citadel's chief executives. Source: Wikipedia, GameStop short squeeze.

title: The 2022 stock market decline
text: The S&P 500 fell 19% in 2022 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 33%. The S&P 500 peaked at 4,796 at the 3 January 2022 close and bottomed about 25% lower in October 2022. Its first six months, down 21%, were the worst start to a year since 1970. On 13 September 2022 it fell 4.32%, its largest single-day drop since June 2020. Source: Wikipedia, 2022 stock market decline.

title: Why stocks fell in the 2022 bear market: inflation and rate rises
text: Wikipedia names the highest inflation readings of the 2021 to 2023 inflation surge and the resulting interest rate rises as the main causes of the 2022 decline. The Federal Reserve raised rates 11 times starting in March 2022 and restarted quantitative tightening in June 2022. It was the worst year for the bond market since 1994. Other factors named were recession fears, an inverted yield curve and supply disruptions from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Source: Wikipedia, 2022 stock market decline.

title: The Federal Reserve (Fed) federal funds rate path from 2022 to 2024: raise, peak, cut
text: The Federal Reserve started raising rates on 16 March 2022 and, per Wikipedia, raised them 11 times starting then. The first hike was 25 basis points, to 0.25% to 0.50%, by an 8 to 1 vote. The federal funds target range peaked at 5.25% to 5.50%, reached on 26 July 2023, and stayed there through 31 July 2024. The Fed began cutting rates on 18 September 2024 with a 50 basis point cut to 4.75% to 5.00%. Source: Wikipedia, 2022 stock market decline; History of Federal Open Market Committee actions.

title: The 2023 stock market rebound (recovery) and AI
text: Stocks recovered in 2023: the S&P 500 rose 24.23% on a price basis, after falling in 2022. Wikipedia credits the start of the AI boom as one factor in the rebound that began in late 2022. The Magnificent Seven stocks accounted for roughly two thirds of the S&P 500's gains in 2023. Sources: Wikipedia, S&P 500; 2022 stock market decline; Magnificent Seven (stocks).

title: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) collapse in March 2023: depositors withdraw billions in a bank run
text: Silicon Valley Bank failed on 10 March 2023 after a bank run. It was the 16th-largest US bank, with $209 billion in total assets at the end of 2022. Customers withdrew $42 billion by the close of 9 March, and another $100 billion was expected the next day. About 89% of its $172 billion in deposits exceeded the FDIC insurance limit. Source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank.

title: Why Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) failed: bonds lost value as interest rates rose
text: Silicon Valley Bank bought long-term securities as deposits grew. When the Federal Reserve raised interest rates, those bonds lost market value, with unrealised losses above $15 billion on held-to-maturity securities at the end of 2022. On 8 March 2023 it announced it had sold over $21 billion of securities, borrowed $15 billion and would sell stock to raise $2.25 billion, which triggered the run. Source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank.

title: Regulators' response and bank stocks after SVB: what the government did
text: On 12 March 2023 the Treasury allowed the FDIC to guarantee uninsured deposits at Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. The Federal Reserve created the Bank Term Funding Program to support other banks. On 13 March 2023 regional bank shares including First Republic, Western Alliance and PacWest fell sharply. US banks lost a combined $100 billion of market value over two days and European banks lost $50 billion. Source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank.

title: The Magnificent Seven (big tech) stocks
text: The Magnificent Seven are Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla. The term was coined in May 2023 by Bank of America analyst Michael Hartnett. The group made up 29% of the S&P 500 by January 2024, and Morgan Stanley put it at 31% by mid-2024. Source: Wikipedia, Magnificent Seven (stocks).

title: Magnificent Seven (big tech) performance and the August 2024 selloff
text: Wikipedia says the Magnificent Seven delivered a 107% return in 2023 and approached a combined $13 trillion valuation in February 2024. On 5 August 2024 the group briefly lost $1 trillion before recovering, with concerns about AI overinvestment cited as a cause. Source: Wikipedia, Magnificent Seven (stocks).

title: Nvidia reaches one, two and three trillion dollars
text: Nvidia became the seventh US company to reach a $1 trillion valuation in 2023. It closed above $2 trillion on 1 March 2024, taking 180 days to go from $1 to $2 trillion, while Apple and Microsoft each took over 500 days. It became the world's most valuable company on 18 June 2024 with a market value above $3.3 trillion. Source: Wikipedia, Nvidia.

title: Nvidia reaches four and five trillion dollars
text: Nvidia first closed above $4 trillion on 10 July 2025, the first company to reach that level. It reached a $5 trillion market value on 29 October 2025, again the first company to do so. Source: Wikipedia, Nvidia.

title: The DeepSeek selloff of January 2025
text: DeepSeek-R1 launched on 20 January 2025, and by 27 January 2025 DeepSeek had overtaken ChatGPT as the most downloaded free app on the US iOS App Store. Wikipedia links this to an 18% drop in Nvidia's stock, meaning its share price. Nvidia lost about $600 billion of market value in one day in January 2025, the largest one-day loss for a US company, attributed to DeepSeek. Sources: Wikipedia, DeepSeek; Nvidia.

title: Nvidia annual revenue growth
text: Nvidia's revenue was about $10.9 billion in fiscal 2020, $16.6 billion in fiscal 2021 and $26.9 billion in fiscal 2022. It was $26.9 billion in fiscal 2023, $60.9 billion in fiscal 2024, about $130 billion in fiscal 2025 and $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended 25 January 2026. Net income in fiscal 2026 was $120.1 billion. Source: Wikipedia, Nvidia.

title: Nvidia and demand for AI chips
text: By 2025 Nvidia controlled more than 80% of the market for GPUs used to train and run AI models. In January 2024 Raymond James estimated an H100 chip sold for $25,000 to $30,000, while individual H100s on eBay cost over $40,000. In November 2024 Morgan Stanley reported that Nvidia's entire 2025 production of Blackwell chips was already sold out. Source: Wikipedia, Nvidia.

title: ChatGPT launch, release date, first model it started with, and adoption
text: ChatGPT was released on 30 November 2022, using the GPT-3.5 model. Wikipedia says it reached 100 million monthly active users two months after its release. GPT-4 was released in March 2023 and GPT-4o in May 2024. Source: Wikipedia, ChatGPT.

title: ChatGPT model releases from 2024 to 2025
text: OpenAI released the o1 model in December 2024 and GPT-4.5 in February 2025. GPT-4.1 and o3 arrived in April 2025, and GPT-5 in August 2025. Source: Wikipedia, ChatGPT.

title: The global chip shortage of 2020 to 2023
text: The global chip shortage ran from 2020 to 2023 and had mostly subsided by 2023. Broadcom's lead times grew to 22.2 weeks in April 2021, up from 12.2 weeks in February 2020. Cars account for about 15% of global chip consumption and an average modern car has 1,400 to 1,500 chips. The shortage was expected to cost the global car industry $210 billion in revenue in 2021. Source: Wikipedia, 2020 to 2023 global chip shortage.

title: What caused the chip shortage
text: Wikipedia names pandemic demand shifts, with remote work and learning raising demand for computers while lockdowns shut some production, and limited fab capacity, with TSMC and Samsung already running at maximum. Events added to it: the 2021 Taiwan drought, the February 2021 Texas winter storm, a March 2021 fire at Renesas and 2022 neon supply limits after Russia invaded Ukraine. The China-US trade war and crypto mining demand for GPUs also contributed. Source: Wikipedia, 2020 to 2023 global chip shortage.

title: The CHIPS and Science Act
text: President Biden signed the CHIPS and Science Act on 9 August 2022. The act's funding appropriates $52.7 billion. Provisions include $39 billion in subsidies for chip manufacturing on US soil and $13 billion for semiconductor research and workforce training. It also created a 25% advanced semiconductor manufacturing tax credit. Subsidy recipients are barred for 10 years from producing chips more advanced than 28 nanometres in China and Russia. Source: Wikipedia, CHIPS and Science Act.

title: Working from home in the US, Census data
text: The US Census Bureau put the share of US workers who usually worked from home at 5.7% in 2019. It was 17.9% in 2021, 15.2% in 2022 and 13.8% in 2023, which is more than 22 million people and more than double the 2019 rate. Source: Wikipedia, Remote work.

title: Remote and hybrid work after the pandemic
text: Economist Nicholas Bloom said in 2023 that about a third of all working days were remote, up from 5% before the pandemic. Gallup found in February 2023 that among US employees who could work remotely, 20% were on-site, 28% fully remote and 52% hybrid. Source: Wikipedia, Remote work.

title: Return-to-office orders
text: In early 2025 the US government ordered millions of federal employees back to offices. Wikipedia says media outlets described employers raising in-office expectations gradually without formal mandates as hybrid creep in 2026. Source: Wikipedia, Remote work.

title: Total tech layoffs in 2022 and 2023
text: A mid-2023 Layoffs.fyi snapshot counted more than 161,000 tech employees laid off at 1,046 companies in 2022. A December 2023 report citing Layoffs.fyi gave about 260,238 tech layoffs across 1,169 companies for 2023. Counts vary by snapshot and only cover companies the tracker follows. Sources: TechCrunch; Business Today.

title: Amazon layoffs in 2022 and 2023
text: Amazon laid off about 18,000 employees in several rounds starting in November 2022 and continuing into early 2023. In March 2023 Amazon announced a further 9,000 layoffs. These are announced cuts as reported, not audited totals. Sources: TechCrunch; Business Today.

title: Meta layoffs in 2022 and 2023
text: Meta's layoffs began in November 2022, when it cut more than 11,000 employees. By one 2023 tracker, about 21,000 people had lost their jobs at Meta since November 2022. These are reported figures, not audited totals. Sources: Yahoo Finance layoffs tracker; TechCrunch.

title: Google layoffs in 2023
text: Google announced plans to lay off about 12,000 employees globally, around 6% of its workforce. The cuts reached divisions including Area 120 and Intrinsic. This is an announced figure as reported, not an audited total. Sources: TechCrunch; Business Today.

title: Amazon Web Services (AWS) and the cloud market: biggest largest cloud provider and market share
text: AWS revenue was about $46 billion at the end of 2020 and $128.7 billion in 2025, with $45.6 billion of operating income in 2025. Synergy Research Group put cloud infrastructure share in the first quarter of 2023 at 31% for AWS, 25% for Microsoft Azure and 11% for Google Cloud. Source: Wikipedia, Amazon Web Services.

title: Zoom after the pandemic boom: IPO, layoffs and Nasdaq-100 removal
text: Zoom's IPO in April 2019 priced at $36 a share, and the stock rose over 72% on its first trading day. In February 2023 it announced a 15% workforce cut, about 1,300 employees. It was removed from the Nasdaq-100 in December 2023. Source: Wikipedia, Zoom Communications.
